hooks.text: A monster solar storm missed erasing our modern world by nine days.
A history-making superstorm hit us, yet nobody on Earth noticed.
What missed wiping out our power grids by only nine days?

title: The Solar Storm That Missed Earth by Nine Days
description: In July 2012, an ultra-fast Carrington-class solar superstorm crossed Earth's orbit, missing us by just nine days and sparing our modern power grids.

beats.text: A monster solar storm missed erasing our modern world by nine days.
beats.visual: NASA SDO satellite capture of a giant solar flare, 2012

beats.text: On July 23, 2012, the Sun launched a massive Carrington-class plasma eruption.
beats.visual: SOHO spacecraft view of an intense coronal mass ejection, 2012

beats.text: This blast traveled at over two thousand kilometers per second, four times faster than normal.
beats.visual: Artist illustration of a coronal mass ejection traveling through space, NASA
queries: coronal mass ejection space illustration NASA

beats.text: It achieved this record speed because an eruption four days earlier had cleared its cosmic path.
beats.visual: Solar Dynamics Observatory view of sequential coronal mass ejections, 2012

beats.text: A direct hit would have crippled global power grids and water pumps, costing over two trillion dollars.
beats.visual: Illustration of Earth's magnetosphere being compressed by a solar storm, NASA

beats.text: Instead, NASA's STEREO-A spacecraft in deep space safely recorded the entire blow.
beats.visual: Artist concept of NASA's STEREO spacecraft in orbit around the Sun, NASA

beats.text: Physicist Pete Riley calculated a twelve percent chance a similar disaster strikes Earth each decade.
beats.visual: Portrait of astronomer Richard Carrington, 19th century

beats.text: We survived only because the erupting region of the Sun was no longer pointed directly at us.
beats.visual: Visualization of the solar storm missing Earth's orbit, NASA
